This is the last molecule my budget can score, and the data now tells me exactly which combination to build. Three effects measured on matched pairs: a cyclopropanecarboxamide cap instead of acetyl is worth about +0.10 of jnk3 and it also gives the best QED I have seen in the series; a 4-methyl on the pyridine is worth about +0.13; and the fluorine on the central ring, which I had wrongly credited for the earlier jump, is actually slightly negative - 0.25 without it versus 0.20 with it on the cyclopropyl pair, and 0.15 versus 0.14 on the acetyl pair. The real driver was always the pyridine. No molecule so far combines the good cap with the pyridine methyl and drops the fluorine, so that is what I will make. Step 1 removes the fluorine: atom 16 is the aromatic carbon carrying it and atom 17 is the fluorine, a non-ring bond.
